conviction_note: FY26 was fully pre-released on 30 Jun and the FY27 guide was raised only six weeks ago (18 Aug), so the release most likely reiterates the guide with 'further colour'. The stock is +48% since 12 Aug (35p to 51.75p) with no guidance-level news since, and in the same setup the last two September finals fell 7.6% and 6.2%. That puts p_up at 44 on an abs move of ~6% (thin two-analyst AIM name, finals-only history 6-8%), which gives about -0.7. I shrank it from the -1.0 draft because the negative largely agrees with the run-up, which is the free control, and there is no short-register anchor to beat.

findings.finding: This release is structurally unlikely to carry a guidance change. FY26 was pre-released on 30 Jun, and the FY27 guide was raised on 18 Aug to £63-66m / £6.3-6.6m with the finals promised only 'further colour'. Meanwhile the stock has risen 48% from 35.0p (12 Aug) to 51.75p. The only operational news since the raise is a framework appointment the company itself says carries 'no guaranteed level of expenditure or revenue'. The implied bar has therefore moved above the company's own guide, and the most likely release (reiteration, Q1 'in line with upgraded expectations') is the setup this name has sold in both previous Septembers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sep 2024 finals (pre-released, reiterated) -7.6% on the day and -10.6% by d+5. Sep 2025 finals ('traded in line with management's expectations in the first quarter', 'confidence in delivering consensus') -6.2% on the day and -13.6% by d+5. By contrast, releases that carried a new upgrade rose: Feb 2026 interims 'materially ahead' +13.5%, Dec 2025 +28.3%, Aug 2026 +11.1%. The sign is decided by whether the guide moves. Per-event moves are in the baseline history, sourced to https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/MTEC.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were pricing a plain reiteration, the stock would sit near the post-upgrade level of about 42-43.5p (18-28 Aug closes) plus some credit for the framework. Instead it is at 51.75p, about 20% higher, with no new guidance. That gap is either a bet on a further upgrade or 'further colour' at the finals, or momentum. On a two-analyst, $0.33m/day AIM name with no disclosed short, nobody is positioned to lean against it. The caveat is that this reading overlaps the run-up (the free control), which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: The reaction pattern comes from the issuer's own prior finals (FY25 finals current-trading wording: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/made-tech-group--mtec/final-results/9127402) and the price path from the Yahoo tape in the baseline. The counter-evidence is the same management's unbroken beat-and-raise record since Jun 2025 (Dec 2025 trading statement https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/made-tech-group--mtec/trading-statement/9286456; Feb 2026 interims https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/made-tech-group--mtec/interim-results/9447660). It is folded into this one finding through p_up 44 rather than filed as a second, opposite-signed finding on the same line.

outside_window.finding: The government's new Insourcing Unit (announced 27 Sep 2026 at Labour conference, sitting in OPMC) and the June 2026 Public Interest Test explicitly target a 'reduction in consultancy and professional services spending', and technology services are in scope for contracts above £1m. This is a structural demand headwind for a UK public-sector digital consultancy. TechMarketView expects it to reshape contracts rather than cause wholesale insourcing. Transmission to Made Tech is unconfirmed by the company, and the stock moved +0.5% on 28 Sep.
The Capital Markets Day is promised 'later in FY27', and more detailed ambitions and targets will come there rather than at the finals.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the lean (-0.95, which is all run-up since there is no short anchor) and with the free control (-run_up_20d, +19%/60d +36%). The only independent content is the issuer's own guide timing and its September-finals reaction history. So the number is kept below the draft and near the size of the lean, rather than stacked on top of it.
language_note: The UK's local half here is source locality, not language, and most of what mattered (the pre-release, the guide raise, the notice of results) was carried identically by the English wires (Alliance News, TipRanks, Proactive) and the RNS originals.

Domestic RNS TR-1s (Investegate) carried the long-side supply the wire copy did not: co-founder Blackburn selling 14.50% to 12.86% on 20 Aug, and Octopus stepping down 5.79% to 4.93% to 3.78% through 2026.

UK trade press (TechMarketView, 28 Sep) carried the government Insourcing Unit and Public Interest Test with explicit intent to cut consultancy spend, a sector headwind I found in no English wire item about Made Tech. It is sized only outside the window because transmission is unconfirmed.

UK government procurement registers (Contracts Finder, Find a Tender) are a domestic primary source for bookings. Here they showed nothing undisclosed, which is itself evidence that Q1 bookings beyond the RNS'd awards are not visible.
lessons_applied: Rule 3/5 (two findings that cannot both be true go to one sign): the draft's -1.3 'reiteration after run-up' and +0.6 'serial beat-and-raise management' were two opposite bets on the same guidance line. They are merged into one guidance finding, with the upgrade chance expressed through p_up (42 to 44).

Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company says it): the draft's -0.3 Insourcing Unit finding was moved to outside_window, since the policy is real but Made Tech has not said it affects demand.

Rule 7 and the EU 'positioning is the thing to beat' and 'truncated zero' rules: with anchor_covered false, the lean IS the run-up, and my negative mostly agrees with it. The finding was shrunk and positioning_check states that there is no anchor.

EU 'let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': abs_move_pct was kept at 6.0 (thin name, pre-released period, prior finals 6-8%) and not cut toward the 2.3% reiteration median. The September-finals history only moves p_up.
